newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 2.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 2. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia marked World AIDS Day on Sunday with day-long performances at the Ancol theme park in north Jakarta. There are offficially only 463 cases of HIV/AIDS in Indonesia but health workers said the real total could be much higher.

Leaders of two of the country's most influential Islamic groupings sat next to each other at a meeting after years of frosty relations. This was seen as a rapprochement between Abdurrahman Wahid of the 30-million strong Nahdlatul Ulama and Amien Rais, head of the Muhammadiyah Islamic grouping.

Police in Yogyakarta have said they are looking for other possible suspects in the murder of a journalist in the central Java city earlier this year. Human rights groups had said the man the police have arrested is not the murderer.

Investigations into the involvement of the new Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) chief, Surjadi, in riots in Jakarta in July will not affect next year's election process, State Secretary Murdiono said. Ousted party chief Megawati Sukarnoputri has said she is the rightful leader of the PDI.
